pages.content:
The Beginning of Human Life

The Stone Age in India marks the beginning of human civilization. Based on the type of tools used, it is divided into three major periods:

  • Paleolithic Age: Old Stone Age (Hunters & Gatherers)
  • Mesolithic Age: Middle Stone Age (Domestication of animals)
  • Neolithic Age: New Stone Age (Agriculture began)

The earliest traces of human existence in India go back to 500,000 BC.

Tools & Lifestyle

Early humans lived in caves and rock shelters. The Bhimbetka Caves in Madhya Pradesh are a famous example of Paleolithic art.

They used tools made of quartzite, which is why Paleolithic men in India are also called 'Quartzite Men'.

Discovery & Extent

The Indus Valley Civilization (IVC) was a Bronze Age civilization (3300–1300 BCE). It extended from present-day Northeast Afghanistan to Pakistan and Northwest India.

Major Sites:

  • Harappa (Punjab, Pakistan)
  • Mohenjo-daro (Sindh, Pakistan)
  • Lothal (Gujarat, India)
  • Kalibangan (Rajasthan, India)

Urban Planning

The most striking feature of Harappan civilization was its town planning. The streets cut each other at right angles (Grid System).

Note: Mohenjo-daro had the 'Great Bath', which was used for ritual bathing.

They used burnt bricks for construction, which was rare in contemporary civilizations like Egypt.

Agriculture & Trade

The Harappans grew wheat, barley, pulses, peas, rice, sesame, linseed, and mustard. They were the first to produce Cotton in the world.

Trade existed with Mesopotamia, where Indus seals have been found.

The Aryan Invasion Theory

The Vedic Age started with the coming of the Aryans. They were semi-nomadic people who came from Central Asia (Max Muller's theory).

They settled in the region of Sapta Sindhu (Land of Seven Rivers).

Vedic Literature

The main source of information for this period is the Vedic literature, which consists of:

  1. The Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda.
  2. The Brahmanas: Commentary on Vedas.
  3. The Aranyakas: Forest books.
  4. The Upanishads: Philosophical texts.

Rigveda is the oldest text in the world.
